children: By Staff Writer
BNW Developments will begin handover of units in its first luxury beachfront projects on Al Marjan Island in Ras Al Khaimah from next year, Chairman and Founder Ankur Aggarwal told Zawya Projects.

“The first keys we hand over will be for our luxury beachfront portfolio on Al Marjan Island, starting with Aqua Arc and Pelagia. Foundations and basements are complete, and the main structures are now rising out of the ground,” he said.
The company purchased its first plots on Al Marjan Island back in 2022.
“Since we made those initial purchases, land values on Al Marjan have soared by anywhere from 150 percent to 200 percent, depending on the exact location and beach access,” Aggarwal said.
BNW Developments remains optimistic about the UAE real estate market and expects branded residences to benefit further from the ongoing regional conflict.

“When people buy a property attached to a name like Taj or Radisson, they know they are buying a trusted, liquid asset that holds its value far better through ups and downs than standard unbranded buildings,” he stated.
Excerpts from the interview:
Ras Al Khaimah’s real estate story has changed dramatically in a short time. How is BNW benefiting from this growth?

What’s happening in Ras Al Khaimah right now is a fundamental shift. RAK has positioned itself as a major investment hub, especially with big developments happening around Al Marjan Island and RAK Central. We moved early, securing prime land in both coastal and commercial zones before the market took off, which really laid the foundation for us to build at scale.

Right now, our project footprint is about 75 percent in Ras Al Khaimah and 25 percent in Dubai. Dubai will always be a core anchor for us. It’s where we focus on boutique high-end luxury. But RAK is where we see the biggest runway for growth, so naturally, that's where most of our large, branded communities are coming to life.
BNW currently holds 45 percent of land parcels in RAK Central. How much has been used and how do you plan to use the remaining landbank?
Holding nearly half of the private land in RAK Central comes with a significant responsibility to get the master planning right.

So far, we have tapped roughly 15 percent to 20 percent of our total space there, starting with flagship projects like our twin development with Radisson Blu. The rest of the landbank will be rolled out gradually over the next three to four years. The plan is to create a true mixed-use business hub - combining prime office space with luxury residential towers, retail centres, and more hotel partnerships to cater to all the companies and executives setting up shop in the emirate.
The majority of your branded projects are on Al Marjan. Do you still hold land in Al Marjan? What kind of land appreciation have you seen since you first acquired land on the island?
Yes, we still hold prime beachfront parcels on Al Marjan Island. We bought our first plots back in 2022 and 2023, well before the island became the key topic it is today.

Since we made those initial purchases, land values on Al Marjan have soared by anywhere from 150 percent to 200 percent, depending on the exact location and beach access. Buyers who came in during our early project launches have already seen capital growth in the 25 percent to 35 percent range. It has turned out to be one of the best-performing micro-markets in the region.
BNW has tied up with Taj, Radisson, Tonino Lamborghini and Fashion TV to launch branded residences in RAK. Can you share some construction details on these projects?

When you work with global hospitality and luxury brands, there is zero room for error on quality. That’s why we brought in MASAH as our main contractor to handle the heavy lifting across our major sites.
Aqua Arc & Pelagia (Al Marjan Island): Piling and foundation works are well advanced, and we are moving right into pouring the main concrete structures above ground.
Taj Wellington Mews & Tonino Lamborghini Residences: The full architecture and engineering designs are complete, and enabling works and excavation are actively happening on-site.
Radisson Blu Hotel & Residences (RAK Central): Deep foundation piling is moving ahead as scheduled to support these high-rise buildings.
We also have independent teams auditing every phase of construction to keep everything on schedule without cutting corners on build quality.
BNW Developments recently announced plans to build 10,000 homes over the next four years. What factors were considered when finalising this plan?
The goal of building 10,000 homes is grounded in a clear understanding of market realities and tangible demand.
People are moving here: The UAE keeps drawing in global business, entrepreneurs, and wealth, while RAK itself is actively pushing to grow its population and tourism footprint.

Global buyer demand: We are seeing massive interest from international buyers, particularly from India, which accounts for around 14.4 percent of our buyers, as well as Europe and the broader Gulf region.
Execution capability: We locked in reliable construction partners early, so we know we have the supply chain and workforce ready to build at this scale.
Land already secured: Because we bought our land early, we aren't squeezed by rising land prices, allowing us to help keep project budgets intact.
Which will be the first project to begin handover? Can you share the construction update on that project?

Our handovers will begin in 2027. The first keys we hand over will be for our luxury beachfront portfolio on Al Marjan Island, starting with Aqua Arc and Pelagia. Foundations and basements are complete, and the main structures are now rising out of the ground.
Following recent regional geopolitical shifts, has there been any change in your outlook on the residential property markets in Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah, particularly the branded residences segment?

Not at all. Our long-term view is as positive as ever. Under the UAE’s strong, forward-looking leadership, the country has built an environment defined by stability, confidence, and long-term opportunity. Whenever there is uncertainty elsewhere in the world, the UAE consistently proves itself as a safe haven. People want to move their families and capital here because of the safety, neutral policy, clear regulations, zero capital gains tax, and Golden Visa options.

Branded residences benefit even more from this environment. When people buy a property attached to a name like Taj or Radisson, they know they are buying a trusted, liquid asset that holds its value far better through ups and downs than standard unbranded buildings.

The appeal of beachfront living goes well beyond price. It is about the quality of the experience: the connection to the water, the sense of space, privacy, and a lifestyle that remains inherently desirable.

What ultimately defines the value, however, is what a developer brings to that setting. Thoughtful design, quality, amenities, service, and a clear vision for how people will live. The beachfront may create the opportunity, but the developer defines its long-term value.
(Reporting by P Deol; Editing by Anoop Menon)
